lesson.menu_desc: Review and integrate Block 3: the third conditional, reported speech, the passive with modals, discourse markers and hedging in one full update followed by questions, then a self-assessment -- plus the words of the decision: go-ahead, fallback, at stake, mandate, leeway, sound out, spell out, walk through, weigh in, follow through
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 30 -- The Big Review -- Block 3 Integration
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Maria Claudia Curimbaba | Lesson 30 -- Review

paras: The call opened with a five-minute update from Maria Claudia Curimbaba on the Pittsburgh line. She said that the May container had been cleared in Santos on the third, after two days of demurrage, and that the documents should have been sent earlier. She took responsibility for that step and said that a second check would be introduced before every container is sealed.

Having said that, she explained that the June consignment was still at risk, because the carrier had changed the route and the lead time was now five weeks. She walked the partners through two options: rerouting the second container through Paranagua, which would cost about USD 2,400 and save nine days, or expediting it, which would cost USD 6,100 and save fourteen. She spelled out one caveat: both figures assumed that the exchange rate stayed where it was.

Tom Reilly asked whether Pittsburgh was still the right supplier for the joint venture. Ms. Curimbaba conceded that a backup supplier was needed, but she said she stood by Pittsburgh for June, as the goods had been ready on time on both occasions. She added that a third delay was unlikely, but that it could not be ruled out.

The partners weighed in on the options. It was agreed that the second container would be rerouted through Paranagua, and Ms. Curimbaba was given a mandate to negotiate the rate with the forwarder up to USD 2,600. She will sound out two backup suppliers and report back by the fifteenth. If the rate is not confirmed by Friday, expediting remains the fallback.

listenings.text: Maria Claudia, Tom Reilly here, following up on this morning's call. First of all, thank you. That was the clearest update we have had on the Pittsburgh line, and two of the partners told me so afterwards. Two things. To begin with, the rerouting through Paranagua has the go-ahead from our side, and your mandate on the forwarder's rate stands at twenty-six hundred dollars. If you can get it lower, even better. Having said that, one of the partners asked me whether the backup suppliers would be able to meet our quality standard, and I told him I did not know. It seems to me that is the first question you should put to them, before price. Finally, when you sound them out, please spell out that this is not a tender yet. We are not looking to replace Pittsburgh this year. Call me when you have the rate.

Three months ago, I needed a colleague on every call with our partners abroad. Today I ran one on my own, and I want to be honest about what worked and what did not. What worked was the structure. I opened with one sentence, I signposted every part, and nobody asked me where we were. What worked less well was the numbers. Twice I said a figure too fast, and I had to repeat it. The questions were the part I was most afraid of, and they turned out to be the part I did best. When I was asked whether I could guarantee the date, I did not say yes. I said it was likely, and I spelled out what it depended on. If I had given that answer three months ago, it would have been in Portuguese, in my head, and it would have arrived too late. Next block, I want to work on one thing only: the pace of my numbers.

extra_audio.text: First, before the meeting, you sound out one person to learn what the others are worried about. Then, you write the outline around the one decision you need from the room. After that, you give the update: a hook, three signposted points and a call to action. Next, you answer the questions, conceding what is true and hedging what you cannot promise. Finally, you follow through: you do what you promised, and you report back by the date you gave.
